title: Mixed-workload calibration drift and throughput/latency benchmarks for FP8/INT8 variants
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description: Run a set of throughput and latency benchmarks to measure operational behavior and accuracy drift for FP8 and INT8 quantized model variants under mixed workloads. Focus areas: long-context requests, bursty multi-tenant traffic, KV cache warm/cold transitions, and batching interactions. Goal is to produce a reproducible matrix of results and a short set of tunable mitigations for serving policies.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark matrix executed for FP8 and INT8 variants across defined batch sizes and context lengths
Measured p50/p90/p99 latencies and tokens-per-second captured in the dashboard
Accuracy deltas (perplexity and task metrics) computed and compared to full-precision baseline
Identification of at least two concrete runtime mitigations with estimated cost/latency trade-offs
Reproducible runbook and scripts checked into github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/quant-drift and referenced in ticket
benchmark_design: Workload mix: 70% small chat requests (<=128 tokens), 20% medium context (512-1024 tokens), 10% long-context (4096-8192 tokens)
Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8, 16 (include both static batching and dynamic continuous batching modes)
KV cache states: cold (no prior requests), warm (after 200 long-context requests), saturated (repeated long-context churn)
Burst scenarios: steady 50 req/s, microburst 300 req/s for 10s every 5 minutes, and multi-tenant isolation test (3 tenants with different request mixes)

Metrics: p50/p90/p99 latency (tail measured at 99.9th for microbursts), tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory pressure, KV-cache hit rate, and quality metrics (perplexity delta, answer-f-score on eval set, embedding cosine similarity)
quality_validation_plan: Use the SDR prompt suite and eval set stored in Drive (drive.redwood.com/quant-evals/2026/mixed-workload) to compute task-level metrics
Compare FP8 and INT8 outputs to float32 baseline using token-level perplexity and semantic similarity (embedding cosine); flag any >3% degradation in key tasks
Run automated diff harness to surface hallucination/formatting regressions for structured output prompts
Manually review 50 failure cases per quant variant to classify degradation mode (calibration bias, saturation, tokenization edge case)
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Initial test matrix drafted; identified required infra changes to the benchmark runner for multi-tenant labels (Ayesha)

2026-02-26: Prototype scripts committed to github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/PR#412; basic FP8/INT8 runs succeed on small sample; observed 6% perplexity increase for INT8 on long-context (Marco)
2026-03-03: Added KV cache warmup harness and microburst generator; noticed p99 tail increase during cache warm transitions for batch sizes >=8 (SRE triage)
2026-03-08: Ran multi-tenant interference test; found cross-tenant cold starts causing KV eviction patterns that disproportionately affect FP8 latency at high memory pressure (investigation ongoing)

2026-03-11: Quant calibration sweep added to pipeline; early results indicate per-layer calibration reduces FP8 perplexity delta by ~1.5% but increases end-to-end latency by ~4% in continuous-batching mode
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: For the public benchmark report we will include both steady-state (KV warm) and transient (KV cold/warm transitions) numbers to capture realistic client behavior
Trade-off: Per-layer calibration improves accuracy but increases compute overhead; recommend offering it as a toggle per deployment tier rather than default in hosted low-latency settings
Mitigation considered: Adaptive batch caps that reduce max batch size during KV-warmup period to limit tail latency; will prototype in next sprint
Open question: Whether to expose per-tenant quant profile selection in Dedicated; requires UX + keying changes in routing layer
